name: New Incentives (The Life You Can Save, 2025)

missing_data.note: Partly thin (50%): New Incentives counts the infants it enrolled, but the deaths and illness are the Lives Saved Tool's estimate of Nigeria's national rise in coverage, credited by New Incentives' share of the country's under-fives rather than the vaccinations it was measured to add.

summary: New Incentives gives mothers in northern Nigeria small cash payments when they bring their infants for routine vaccinations. The Life You Can Save credits it with its share (by infants enrolled) of the child deaths and illness that Nigeria's rise in vaccine coverage from 2022 to 2024 averted, from the Lives Saved Tool and the literature, at New Incentives' $17 per infant. Our view values the deaths the site's way, counts illness for as long as it lasts and cuts tuberculosis to New Incentives' share; the biggest uncertainty is whether the national coverage gain is a fair measure of what New Incentives added.

sections.title: New Incentives' share of Nigeria's under-fives

sections.title: Deaths averted
sections.explainer: The Lives Saved Tool (LiST) estimates the child deaths averted by Nigeria's rise in vaccine coverage from 2022 to 2024; the sheet credits New Incentives with its share.

sections.title: Illness averted
sections.explainer: Cases of diarrhoea, pneumonia and meningitis from LiST; tuberculosis, diphtheria, whooping cough, hepatitis B and measles from figures in the literature and the rise in coverage.

Value of averting a child's death, in healthy years
rows.explainer: **Changed for consistency.** The Life You Can Save counts a death averted as life expectancy at birth discounted at 3% (28.9 years). The site values every child's death the same way: GiveWell's moral weight for a death under five times the value-of-a-life slider, in healthy years.

rows.label: Length of an acute episode of illness
rows.explainer: A disability weight is a share of a year of healthy life lost while ill, so the years lived with disability are cases × weight × how long a case lasts. The sheet leaves the length out (a full year per case). Diarrhoea, pneumonia, meningitis, diphtheria, acute hepatitis B and measles last days to a few weeks, whooping cough up to two months; our judgment, 0.03 years (about 11 days, 4 days to 5 weeks).

rows.label: Length of a child's tuberculosis episode
rows.explainer: From the first symptoms through diagnosis and six months' treatment; our judgment, a year (six months to two years).

rows.label: Years lived with disability averted, tuberculosis, New Incentives' share
rows.explainer: **Correction.** The sheet credits New Incentives with the tuberculosis cases the national rise in BCG coverage averted among all Nigeria's children; every other illness is cut to its share of the under-fives, and so is this one here.

rows.label: Years lived with disability averted, with lengths of illness
Protection of unvaccinated children by those vaccinated, as a share of the result
rows.explainer: Vaccinated children pass on less measles, pneumococcus, Hib and whooping cough to others; the sheet counts only the children enrolled. Our judgment, 10% (0 to 30%).

rows.label: Share of the credited coverage gain due to New Incentives
rows.explainer: The sheet credits New Incentives with the national coverage gain in proportion to the under-fives it enrolled, not with the vaccinations it was measured to add. We keep the sheet's attribution (×1), with a range down to half for the chance that its children would have shared in the national rise anyway.
